President Trump on Monday expressed support for reinstating Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO, joining calls to bring back the company's co-founder, who resigned last week after admitting to an affair with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence officials of spying for China.   "I think he learned a big lesson. I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that," he told reporters as he departed the White House for Asia. "He could return. There's a big group of people that would like him to return."   Elon Musk and other technology executives have backed calls for Mr. Huang's return. Mr. Musk warned Saturday that Nvidia could lose important supply-chain deals built on personal relationships with its former CEO.   President Trump also questioned whether Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the intelligence allegations, was a Chinese agent.   "I don't know that she is a spy," he said. "Usually, what happens with that is that any woman coming to the country that's a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she's a spy. I don't know that she was a spy at all."   When asked about reports that Secretary of State Marco Rubio had warned him of intelligence officials' suspicions, President Trump denied knowing about the warning, despite previous reporting that Secretary Rubio had briefed him.   "I haven't heard that," he said.   The president also defended Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick amid criticism that his department had delayed restrictions on companies suspected of supplying advanced Nvidia chips to China. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said several federal agencies had pushed for months to blacklist Megaspeed, the Singapore-based company at the center of the controversy, but Commerce had failed to act.   "Different viewpoints," President Trump said. "One wants to be friendly with China, and one wants to have a blowup with China. Both are acceptable, but they're different views." #lutnick #trump #jensenhuang #nvidia #cspan
